title: Harbor and Summer
premise: Hazel Montrose has built a careful life ghostwriting other people's truths, including the memoirs of her rival, celebrated novelist Margot Ashford. When a letter Hazel wrote eleven years ago — and never sent — surfaces in a dead man's estate, it exposes the summer she spent in Harbor Bay with Jonah Reyes, the man she loved and abandoned to protect her family's secret complicity in a wrongful conviction. The letter pulls her back to Harbor Bay, where Jonah now fights to clear his brother's name, and where Margot's memoir threatens to bury the truth forever. Torn between loyalty to her employer, the law's slow machinery, and the justice only truth can deliver, Hazel must choose: publish what she knows and destroy her career, or stay silent and lose Jonah a second time. She chooses truth — testifying at last, losing everything but herself — and in the wreckage finds that love, honestly told, can begin again.
about_author: Ulyana Ravensworth is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent a decade listening to other people's confessions before writing her own. She lives on a fog-bound coast where she collects unsent letters and writes about the courage it takes to send them.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Hand
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In her Manhattan apartment, Hazel finishes a chapter of Margot Ashford's memoir in Margot's voice, erasing herself from every sentence. A call from her agent confirms another lucrative contract. Emotional beat: the hollow competence of a woman fluent in everyone's story but her own.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. An estate lawyer contacts her: among a dead client's papers is an unsent letter bearing Hazel's handwriting, addressed to Jonah Reyes. Her blood runs cold; she thought it destroyed. Emotional beat: dread as the past knocks with a key she thought she'd changed.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with flashback fragments. Rereading the letter, Hazel relives the summer in Harbor Bay — Jonah, his brother Tomás's arrest, and the lie she told to shield her father. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing like a body that was never allowed to sink.

chapters.title: Margot's Version
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. At her Connecticut estate, Margot reviews the memoir draft and recognizes Harbor Bay in Hazel's prose. She begins quietly investigating her ghostwriter. Emotional beat: elegant possessiveness — Margot collects stories, and now she wants this one.

chapters.title: The Road Back
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Claiming 'research,' Hazel drives to Harbor Bay, telling herself it's about the letter, not the man. The town is gentrified but the harbor unchanged. Emotional beat: fear braided with longing as familiar streets undo eleven years of discipline.

chapters.title: Jonah
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah, now running a boatyard and a one-man fight to reopen Tomás's case, spots Hazel at the marina diner. Eleven years of anger and unfinished love collide in a civil conversation that cuts both of them. Emotional beat: the shock of a wound still bleeding after all this time.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Hazel offers to help Jonah find evidence; he refuses her help but can't refuse her presence. They agree to uneasy cooperation — nothing personal. Emotional beat: two people negotiating a truce their hearts never signed.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Papers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Digging into the estate, Hazel learns the deceased was the retired harbormaster who witnessed the night Tomás was arrested — and that someone else has been asking for his files. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by the sense of being hunted.

chapters.title: Old Loyalties
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Her father calls, sensing trouble, reminding her of the promise that bought her freedom from scandal. Hazel lies to him smoothly and hates how easy it is. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited silence pressing on her chest.

chapters.title: Salt and Memory
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Working late on the boatyard, Jonah and Hazel fall into old rhythms — shared coffee, half-finished sentences. He tells her about the years without her; she almost tells him about the letter. Emotional beat: tenderness rekindling against both their wills.

chapters.title: Margot Arrives
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Margot descends on Harbor Bay under the guise of 'coastal research' for her memoir, charming the town and cornering Hazel with a velvet threat: she knows who Hazel loved, and memoirs sell better with scandal. Emotional beat: cold fear dressed in warm hospitality.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Log
chapters.summary: Hazel and Jonah's POV, alternating. They recover the harbormaster's logbook from a storage locker; its entries contradict the police timeline of Tomás's arrest. But pages are missing — cut out. Emotional beat: hope arriving torn, proof within reach and just out of grasp.

chapters.title: What Hazel Knew
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Confronted by a log entry naming her father's firm, Jonah demands the truth. Hazel confesses: her father buried evidence to protect a client, and she stayed silent to protect her father. Emotional beat: betrayal and relief tangled — the truth hurts less than its absence.

chapters.title: The Middle of It
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Shattered by Jonah's withdrawal, Hazel realizes the surfaced letter wasn't accident or chance: someone sent it to pull her back. She starts tracing who had access to the estate. Emotional beat: turning from pursued to pursuer.

chapters.title: Tomás
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV, from prison via a visit. Wry and worn, Tomás tells Hazel he stopped hoping years ago — then asks her, of all people, why she came back. Her answer surprises them both. Emotional beat: grace offered where judgment was expected.

chapters.title: The Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Hazel and Jonah's POV. The trail leads to Margot: she obtained the missing pages years ago as research for a novel, and they name the real culprit — a respected local businessman now bankrolling Margot's memoir. Emotional beat: horror as the rival's book becomes the crime's alibi.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Margot offers Hazel a devil's bargain: finish the memoir, keep the pages buried, share the profits — or be exposed as the ghostwriter behind Margot's 'genius.' Hazel's career, her father, and Tomás all hang on one choice. Emotional beat: the loneliest hour, when every door costs something.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter, Sent
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel finally gives Jonah the original letter — the whole unedited truth of why she left and what she sacrificed. He reads it in silence while she waits on his doorstep. Emotional beat: naked vulnerability; love offered without terms for the first time.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Margot's publisher announces the memoir's release date — the same week as Tomás's final appeal hearing. Whoever controls the story controls the verdict. Hazel races to authenticate the pages before the book makes them fiction. Emotional beat: breathless escalation, time literally running out.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Climax. Hazel takes the stand, sacrificing her anonymity, her contract, and her father's reputation to present the harbormaster's testimony and pages. Margot's businessman patron unravels under cross-examination. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into power — a woman finally speaking in her own voice.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Tomás walks free into the harbor light. Margot, exposed, retreats; her memoir dies unpublished. Hazel's father faces consequences and, for once, doesn't ask her to lie. Jonah and Hazel stand at the water's edge, everything lost except what matters. Emotional beat: quiet devastation blooming into peace.

chapters.title: Harbor and Summer
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue. One year later, Hazel publishes her first novel under her own name — the true story, lightly veiled. On the dock at dusk, Jonah slips a new letter into her hands: this one addressed, stamped, and signed with tomorrow. Emotional beat: the past tense finally becoming present — love kept, not lent.
